title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Emily Carter
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding, integration handoffs, escalation handling, ongoing health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and the GTM account team.

Scope and objectives:
- Scope: Applies to new enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private deployments) and major integrations for existing customers.
- Objectives: Ensure a predictable onboarding experience, fast time-to-value, efficient escalation resolution, and continuous service health monitoring tied to business outcomes.

Key outcomes we aim for:
1. First production inference in customer environment within 6 weeks for Dedicated and 8 weeks for Private deployments (typical).
2. Clear escalation timelines and ownership for P1/P2 incidents.
3. Standardized QBR artifacts and health dashboards shared quarterly.

Roles & ownership:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): commercial relationship, QBR ownership, executive escalation path.
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): technical onboarding lead, runbooks, integration validation.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): initial architecture review and integration pattern design.
- Support Engineer (SEng): L2/L3 support, incident handling, remediation.
- Product/Eng owner: triage for product bugs and roadmap requests.

Onboarding checklist (high-level, numbered procedure):
1. Pre-engagement (Account set-up)
   1.1. Contract & access: Confirm contract signed, region and deployment type (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and legal/contractual requirements (DPA, SOC2 if needed).
   1.2. Kickoff call: Schedule 60-90 minute kickoff with CSM, CSE, SE, customer engineering leads.
   1.3. Success criteria: Document measurable success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, cost per inference goals).

2. Architecture & security review
   2.1. Review network requirements for Dedicated/Private (VPC peering, firewall rules, allowed IP ranges).
   2.2. Key management & secrets: Confirm KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments; define rotation policy.
   2.3. Compliance controls: Confirm data residency and retention policies.

3. Integration & validation
   3.1. Credentials & API access: Provide API keys or service accounts, and validate auth flows with a smoke test. Example curl smoke test:

   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Test inference"}'

   3.2. SDK verification: Walk through one of our SDK quickstarts (Python/Node) and confirm sample request/response.
   3.3. Latency & throughput baseline: Run benchmark harness (recommended default: 5 concurrent clients, 1000 short requests) and record p50/p95/p99.

4. Pre-production run & cutover
   4.1. Canary rollout: Configure canary traffic (10% traffic for 48-72 hours) with tracing enabled.
   4.2. Acceptance criteria: No critical errors, p95 latency within agreed SLO, token cost within tolerance.
   4.3. Cutover & monitoring: Increase routing to 100% and hand off to CSM for BAU.

Integration guide (components and configuration table):
| Component | Recommended config / examples | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| API Authentication | Use service account + scoped API key. Example: Create key with role 'inference-client' | CSE | Rotate keys every 90 days unless customer-managed KMS used |
| Network | Allowlist Redwood egress IP range: 3.45.120.0/24 (example). For Private: configure VPC peering and route tables as in reference-arch. | SE | Validate MTU and NAT gateway settings |
| Telemetry | Enable request-level tracing. Export to customer OTLP endpoint or Redwood Console. | CSE | Include trace-id in support tickets |
| Logging & Audits | Enable audit logging for API calls and KMS events. Retention default 90 days. | Customer IT | Provide S3/Blob target or integrate with SIEM |

Configuration snippet (example JSON for an integration manifest):
{
  "deployment": "dedicated",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "network": {"vpc_id":"vpc-0abc1234","allowlist": ["3.45.120.0/24"]},
  "auth": {"key_type": "service_account","scopes": ["inference:invoke"]}
}

Escalation playbook (levels, SLAs, and runbook):
- Severity definitions:
  - P1 (Critical): Platform down for customer or complete data loss. Target initial response: 15 minutes. Target mitigation ETA: 2 hours.
  - P2 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., >30% error rate, sustained p95 latency > SLO). Initial response: 30 minutes. Mitigation ETA: 24 hours.
  - P3 (Medium): Feature degraded or intermittent errors. Initial response: 4 business hours.
  - P4 (Low): Non-urgent feature requests or minor issues. Response in 2 business days.

Escalation steps (numbered):
1. Triage by Support Engineer (L1/L2)
   1.1. Collect required artifacts: request-id, timestamps, p95/p99 latency, recent deploys, error logs, sample payload. Use template in support ticket.
2. If P1/P2, notify CSE and CSM immediately and open a Zoom bridge.
3. If suspected product bug, assign to Product/Eng with priority tag and provide reproducible repro.
4. For infrastructure incidents (capacity, networking), engage Eng-SRE on-call and reference runbook: "SRE: capacity ramp and mitigation".

Contacts & communication channels:
- Support queue (primary): support@redwood.ai (monitored 24x7)
- CSE escalation channel: #cse-escals (Slack)
- On-call Eng-SRE: follow pager rota (pager duty)
- Executive escalation: CSM -> Head of Customer Success -> VP GTM

Required ticket template fields (copy into Zendesk/Jira):
- Customer name, account ID, deployment type
- Severity level, first seen, steps to reproduce
- Request IDs, sample payloads, relevant logs (attach zipped logs <= 50MB)
- Business impact statement

Known issues & workarounds (select examples):
- Symptom: Intermittent 429/RateLimitExceeded on sustained bursts.
  Workaround: Enable client-side exponential backoff with jitter. For Dedicated customers, request temporary burst capacity via support and configure autoscale_policy: "burst: true, max_instances: +20%".
- Symptom: Increased p99 latency after model update.
  Workaround: Roll back to previous model tag (e.g., redwood-1.2 -> redwood-1.1) and open regression ticket with model-onboarding team.
- Symptom: Private deployment audit logs missing for select requests.
  Workaround: Verify KMS permissions and audit-exporter service status (systemctl status audit-exporter). Restart service if failed and escalate to eng-private-deployments if persists.

Health checks & QBR materials:
- Quarterly cadence: CSM schedules QBRs every 90 days with the customer executive sponsor and engineering leads.
- Core health metrics to include in QBR:
  - Availability (monthly uptime %), target >= 99.9%
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 for production traffic, compared to SLOs
  - Error rate: request-error% (5xx), target < 0.5%
  - Cost metrics: cost per 1k tokens & overall monthly inference spend vs. forecast
  - Throughput: average & peak RPS, batch sizes distribution
  - Model quality regressions: evaluation suites run and result deltas

Dashboard and report templates:
- Redwood Console: Use the customer-specific dashboard named "<account-id>-health". Provide read-only viewer link to customer.
- QBR slide template (high level):
  1. Executive summary (past quarter wins + risks)
  2. Usage & adoption (metrics)
  3. Performance & reliability (SLOs vs actual)
  4. Cost analysis & optimization opportunities
  5. Roadmap & feature requests (customer impact)
  6. Action items & owners

Operational checklists (weekly/monthly):
- Weekly: Verify active incidents, top 10 customers by growth, and queue backlog.
- Monthly: Review audit logs retention, billing anomalies, and scheduled upgrade windows.
